AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: Chronic pain is a common problem in the United States, one for which there is a dearth of effective treatments. Nonpharmacological options are a promising alternative, especially for Spanish-speaking Latinos. This pilot study would like to assess the feasibility of an adapted Integrative Medical Group Visit (IMGV) curriculum for a Spanish-speaking Latino chronic pain population.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN AND INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: We translated and adapted the curriculum of the IMGV for a Spanish-speaking Latino chronic pain population. We then tested the feasibility of using this model with two pilot groups (N = 19) using a pre-postdesign.

AbstractText.Label: SUBJECTS
AbstractText.content: This intervention was targeted for underserved Spanish-speaking Latino patients with chronic pain.

AbstractText.Label: SETTINGS/LOCATION
AbstractText.content: This study took place at a safety net academic teaching hospital, the Boston Medical Center, and at a community health center located in a majority Latino neighborhood, the East Boston Neighborhood Health Clinic.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOME MEASURES
AbstractText.content: We used the validated Spanish translations of the Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS-29) (short version), Personal Health Questionnaire (PHQ-8), and Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10). We also gathered qualitative information through focus groups and in-depth interviews.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Using PROMIS measures, there was a statistically significant reduction in pain interference (p = 0.01), fatigue (p = 0.01), and depression (p = 0.01). Qualitative data also indicated the participants felt they benefited from the visits and having care in Spanish was unique.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: This model offers a promising nonpharmacological option for Spanish-speaking patients with chronic pain and could offer an alternative for addressing disparities for this population.
